Furthermore, the application we considered is described by a time independent static model. In fact, dynamic graphical models, namely dynamic Bayesian networks, theory does exist. The structure of this graphical model encodes conditional independence properties between the variables of the model in each time step and also across time steps. This representation is especially useful when reasoning about a system whose state changes over time [22]. The mapping problem is such an example because it involves moving robots whose positions change over time. The application of message-passing procedures to infer in such problems also offers an interesting research subject.
